rationale: The candidate reads as one primary mass with a consistent oblique cut language, but it is still overly tower-like and only partially resolved in section. The visible void/terrace gesture is present, yet it does not become a strong public ground condition at the access edge. Across the four views the mass is coherent enough to avoid total fragmentation, but the form remains closer to an abstract prismatic object with a clipped corner than to a neighborhood-living building with an active threshold and usable public void. The top/opposite views suggest the same volume, so there is no obvious multi-view collision problem, but the section logic is too weak for the program: the roof and upper transformations do not convincingly organize inhabited terraces or a clear public street interface. The best rescue would be to preserve the dominant oblique anchor while carving a more explicit access-side void or terrace and reducing the generic tower character.
